articles.title: Rotating a database password without a restart: how our Redis and Valkey Kubernetes operator works
articles.excerpt: Our free plan has no disk, so Valkey runs with appendonly no and save "", so when the pod restarts, the customer's data is gone. That one fact shaped most of our Kubernetes operator. If rotating a pas…
articles.body: Our free plan has no disk, so Valkey runs with appendonly no and save "" , so when the pod restarts, the customer's data is gone. That one fact shaped most of our Kubernetes operator. If rotating a password restarts the pod, a routine security task wipes someone's cache. So, as expected, we split configuration into two classes: changes that need a restart, and changes that must never cause one. This post walks through how the operator works and why it's built this way, including the parts that aren't finished. Disclosure: this is the operator behind KVNest , the managed Redis and Valkey service we run. Versions and numbers are as of November 2026. TL;DR One cluster-scoped custom resource becomes up to nine child objects, nearly all in a dedicated namespace.

articles.title: I connected Claude to my SEO data. Here's the setup, and what to ask it
articles.excerpt: MCP (Model Context Protocol) removes the copying. It's an open standard that lets an assistant like Claude or ChatGPT call tools on a server you've connected, so it can read your data itself instead o…
articles.body: Every SEO tool I've used has the same workflow. Open the dashboard, find the chart that moved, export it, paste it into a chat window, then ask the AI what it means. The AI is good at the "what it means" part. The copying is the job nobody signed up for. MCP (Model Context Protocol) removes the copying. It's an open standard that lets an assistant like Claude or ChatGPT call tools on a server you've connected, so it can read your data itself instead of waiting for you to paste it. I build Ranklogs , an SEO platform, so full disclosure: this walkthrough uses our MCP server. The setup steps work the same way for any remote MCP server with sign-in. What you need A Ranklogs account. The 14-day trial works and needs no card.

articles.body: 42歳、弱視と向き合うエンジニアの記録：HNのエッセイが背中を押した日 42歳、弱視と向き合うエンジニアの記録：HNのエッセイが背中を押した日 のエッセイ『Resisting Cognitive Surrender』が178ポイントで話題になっていたのを、通勤電車のなかで読んだ。AIに思考を委ねず、認知的主体性を取り戻せというその言葉が、妙に胸に残った。 5歳で左眼弱視（lazy eye）と診断され、アイパッチを貼らされた記憶がある。小学校低学年まで続けたが、「臨界期を過ぎたら治らない」と医師に言われ、以来諦めていた。立体視（ステレオプシス）は一生縁のないものだと思い込んでいた。 しかし、成人でも視覚皮質が再編成されるという神経可塑性の知見を、Meta Quest上で実装したのが Amblyotube だ。仕組みはシンプル：ヘッドセットを被り、YouTubeを再生するだけ。裏では、優位眼（右眼）に調整可能なデジタルぼかし（Dominant Eye Shader）を、弱視眼（左眼）には AI Sharpener（MFBF モード）で人物検出ベースの赤い輪郭・黄緑ハイライト・リズミカルなフリッカーを適用。楔状遮蔽（Wedge Occlusion）で各眼にユニークな視野領域を割り当て、両眼競合を抑制。マゼンタ融合キュー（弱視眼側）と中性グレードット（優位眼側）が脳内で融合を促す。 1日30–40分、好きな動画を見ながら続けられる。3ヶ月目、久しぶりにキャッチボールをしたとき、ボールの距離感が「違う」と感じた瞬間があった。 「手遅れ」という物語に降伏しない。自分の視覚機能を、自分の手でアップデートする。 https://www.meta.com/en-gb/experiences/amblyotube/25906906972338493/

articles.body: Short answer: For a news monitoring service, use staged retrieval architecture with explicit collections, bounded queries, and source context that a reviewer can trace. I build tools for other developers, so the first question is not which vector database has the longest feature list. It is whether an evaluation set can catch a bad result before a newsroom sees it. For a news monitoring service, index cost at scale is the constraint that changes the design. 1. How should evaluation sets shape news monitoring retrieval architecture? Write down the user-visible answer before choosing a vector collection. A query such as “which companies mentioned the rate decision this morning?” needs a time window, tenant boundary, source identity, and a citation. Those fields become a retrieval contract.

articles.body: AI 智能体正在替用户浏览网页、购物和办理事务。对网站而言，它可能看起来与普通用户没有区别，也可能表现为一个承载大量用户请求的统一访客。 核心问题是： 网站看到了智能体，却未必看得到它背后的人。 这会影响个性化服务、风险控制和责任认定；出现问题时，网站往往还需要承担主要处理成本。 对于关注 AI 应用落地的开发者，以及 写好标智库 的技术读者，这个问题值得从系统设计层面讨论：当执行操作的一方不再等于发出指令的一方，网站应如何判断授权、建立信任并保留责任边界？ 远程智能体是一种新的中间服务 本文讨论的个人 AI 智能体，是指接受用户指令，通过控制云端计算机或浏览器完成任务的自动化程序。它们通常由运营方托管和维护，不包括运行在用户本机或本地浏览器中的智能体。 远程智能体位于用户与网站之间：网站直接接触的是智能体，而不一定是用户。云浏览器、代理服务和 VPN 也具有类似的中间服务特征。 区别在于，智能体可以持续运行、并行执行任务，也能承受人类通常不会接受的操作阻力。这让网站过去围绕人类行为建立的容量规划、风控和商业模式面临新的挑战。 如果智能体流量持续增长，简单封禁中间服务就会越来越难以维持。网站需要回答的问题将变成： 在无法直接观察用户的情况下，如何判断是否信任智能体及其运营方？ 一个代办员，就能说明问题 设想一名代办员，同时为几位客户购物、预约和办理手续。 过去，杂货店老板认识每位客户，知道他们各自的偏好。现在只有代办员来下单，老板很难分清订单背后的人。 如果一位客户购买手机后否认授权，商店需要证明交易确实得到客户同意，但商店接触过的只有代办员。 如果另一位客户交给代办员一串密码，让她逐一尝试登录银行，银行能够发现异常尝试，却可能只能封禁代办员，连带影响其他正常客户。 把代办员换成 AI 智能体，把商店和银行换成网站，就能看到同样的矛盾： 封禁整个中间服务可能误伤正常用户；直…

The new model promises better visual consistency, improved reference adherence, more natural speech, and multi-turn conversational editing. articles.title: Earth has captured a new mini moon  — but it won't stick around for long
articles.excerpt: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and QQ8 is sticking around for Christmas.
articles.body: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and it is sticking around for Christmas. The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29). The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027. Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun . QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 5, 2002: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by Jupiter moon Almathea only to find it's a 'pile of icy rubble less dense than water'
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft flew by a small moon called Amalthea and made a surprising find. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft was almost out of fuel. But the Jupiter mission still had some science to do. Galileo flew by a small moon called Amalthea. Amalthea is small, but it's interesting for scientists. The Jupiter moon Amalthea is the reddest object in our solar system. It also generates more heat than it gets from the sun. Scientists think Amalthea creates electrical currents as it orbits in Jupiter's huge magnetic field. Near this little moon, strong radiation from Jupiter is dangerous for spacecraft. The flyby caused some problems for Galileo. The spacecraft went into safe mode only 30 minutes after going past Amalthea. NASA said it was ready for problems, because Galileo was on its last legs, and the radiation near Amalthea was strong.

articles.title: You don't have to go to the moon to see Earth differently: Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover on what really matters
articles.excerpt: After a record-breaking journey around the moon, Artemis 2 astronaut Victor Glover explains why you don't need to travel into space to see Earth differently.
articles.body: TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Imagine traveling over 250 million miles from home, watching Earth disappear behind the moon and losing contact with the billions of people who call it home. What would you miss most? For Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover, the answer wasn't a particular place, a familiar view or even the comforts of home. It was something much more fundamental: human connection. Speaking during a discussion with former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival on Oct. 18 in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Glover reflected on the extraordinary experience of traveling around the moon and how being so far from Earth had given him a renewed appreciation for the people living on it. "The greatest reason to go to space, it isn't to be a swashbuckler hero," Glover said.

articles.excerpt: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is back in communication after the 49-year-old spacecraft briefly fell silent last month, during its interstellar-space mission.
articles.body: Voyager, 1, humanity's most distant spacecraft, is back in contact after briefly losing touch with Earth last month. The spacecraft stopped phoning home for about 48 hours between Oct. 18 and 20 due to a communications glitch that Voyager 1 resolved on its own, before engineers could send the long-running spacecraft a remote fix. "This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected," Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), said in an agency statement about the incident on Oct. 29.
